title: Knowledge of God
lead: In the Hebrew Bible to "know" God means to be in a relationship of loyalty and obedience with him, shown in justice and mercy, not only to hold facts about him. Hosea makes "knowledge of God" the sum of what Israel lacks and will have, and Jeremiah and Isaiah make it the mark of the new covenant and the new age.

sections.b: The verb yada' covers knowing a fact, knowing a person and sexual intimacy. Jeremiah explains the knowledge of God by a king's justice to the poor (Jeremiah 22:16). In the new covenant of Jeremiah 31:34 all will know the LORD, and in Isaiah 11:9 the earth will be full of the knowledge of the LORD. Hosea uses it for what Israel lacks (4:1, 6), will have (2:20) and is told to pursue (6:3).
sections.refs: Hosea 2:20; Hosea 4:1; Hosea 6:3; Jeremiah 22:16; Jeremiah 31:34; Isaiah 11:9; John 17:3
